               <ns0:head>CHAP. XVI.</ns0:head>
               <ns0:p>THese things have I spoken unto you, that ye should not be offended <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">That is, when you see these storms of persecution a<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rise, and fall heavily upon you, they may not give you any occasion, or be any temptation to you to desist from your duty, and be afraid, or ashamed to own me, and the pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fession of my Gospel. Evils unthought of, we are not or<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dinarily prepared for, so as being surprized by them, they the more sink us: <ns0:hi>Offending</ns0:hi> here therefore may signifie, either immoderate trouble and affliction, or being tempted to any Apostacy, or remission of duty.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="2">2 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 9.2<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>, 34. and 12.42.</ns0:note> They shall put you out of the synagogues <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">The term <ns0:hi>Synagogue,</ns0:hi> as it is used often in Scripture to signifie those places of publick Worship which they had in Country Towns and Cities, is proper to the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi>; but as it signifieth an assembly of people met together in any place, it as well agreeth to other people as to them. Our Lord here, in pursuit of the argument which he hath been upon from the 18 verse of the former Chapter, forewarneth his Disciples, that when he should be taken from them, the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> first should Excommunicate them as Hereticks, or Schismaticks: and I know not why, what our Saviour here saith, may not also be extended as a Prophecy of what hath since been done, and is yet doing under the Tyranny of the Pope.</ns0:note>: yea, the time cometh, that whosoever killeth you will think that he doth God service <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">As also the latter clause, which, tho at first was applicable to the <ns0:hi>Iews,</ns0:hi> who stoned <ns0:hi>Stephen</ns0:hi> upon a charge of blasphemy; in which it is apparent, that they thought they did God good service, and doubtless slew many others, yet certainly it also referred to others; even as many as shall do the same thing to the end of the World.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="3">3 And <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 15.21. 1 Cor. 2.8.</ns0:note> these things will they do unto you, because they have not known the Father, nor me <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">This is but what our Lord said as to his Father, <ns0:hi>ver.</ns0:hi> 21. of the former <ns0:hi>Chapter,</ns0:hi> (see the notes on that Verse) and teacheth us, That all persecutions of good men speak in persecutors an ignorance both of God the Father, and of Christ; and who ever they are that continue in such igno<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rance under the light of the Gospel, tho they be baptized, and make never so great a profession of Religion, yet will be under daily temptations to turn persecutors; for ignorance is here made the cause of persecution. And it is some alle<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />viation of trouble to Gods suffering people, to consider that the persons that are the cause of their sufferings, neither know God the Father, nor Jesus Christ; and it is no wonder if they know not God, that they will not know, love, nor approve of them.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="4">4 But <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 13.19. and 14.29.</ns0:note> these things have I told you, that when the time shall come, ye may remember that I told you of them <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">Whatsoever I have discovered to you formerly, of my going to my Father, the coming of the Holy Ghost, your <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="3 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>•••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>fering from the World I have told you of before; you will see that they will most certainly come to pass: then you will remember what I have said unto you, and I have told you them on purpose, that you may remember them, and thereby know, that altho I am in the form of a man, yet I also am God blessed for ever: and did know things that should afterward come to pass, and could tell you the truth about them.</ns0:note>. And <ns0:note n="‡" place="margin">See Matth. 9.15.</ns0:note> these things I said not unto you at the beginning, because I was with you <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">And having been with you, I have not from the first of your converse with me, told you these things; that is, those which relate to the Worlds dealing with you, (which he had told them <ns0:hi>Matth</ns0:hi> 10.16. <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi> but that was after some good whiles converse with them) nor yet had he spo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ken to them at first about his Death, Resurrection, and As<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cension, because <ns0:hi>he was with them,</ns0:hi> and to stay with them some time, during which time he bare the brunt of all; the whole hatred of the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> was poured out upon him: and for those other things relating to his Death, and Ascension, and the sending of the Spirit; he who taught his Disciples, <ns0:hi>Mar.</ns0:hi> 4.33. as they were able to bear them, had concealed these things; till by his other Doctrine he had prepared them to receive this Revelation; and there was a necessity of his relieving them against his bodily absence, by the promise of that other Comforter the Holy Ghost.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="5">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:363" />5 But now I go my way to him that sent me <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">Tho I did not tell you this from the beginging for many wise reasons; yet I now tell you, that I must die, but shall rise again from the dead, and go to my Father who sent me into the World to finish that work which I now have done, and so am returning from whence I came.</ns0:note>, and none of you asketh me, Whither goest thou <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">And tho in<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />deed some of you have cursorily asked me, whither I go, (as <ns0:hi>Peter, Chap</ns0:hi> 13.36.) yet none of you seem to understand, or so seriously as you ought to inquire, whither I go, or so much to be busied in the thoughts of that.</ns0:note>?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="6">6 But becau<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                     <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                  </ns0:gap>e I have said these things unto you, sorrow hath filled your heart <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">But a<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>

               <ns0:p n="7">7 Nevertheless, I tell you the truth; It is expedi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ent for you that I go away <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">He doth not say it was expedient for him, tho this was truth; for his human Nature was not till his Ascension glo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rified, as afterward, <ns0:hi>Chap.</ns0:hi> 17.5. but he saith it was <ns0:hi>expedi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ent for them.</ns0:hi> The Saints may desire a dissolution, but it is for their own advantage, <ns0:hi>Phil.</ns0:hi> 1.23.                <ns0:p n="18">18 They said therefore, What is this that he saith, A little while? we cannot tell what he saith <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">Still they do not understand what he meant. Had not the Disciples reasonable Souls? will any say they had no mind to under<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stand them? certainly none can say so. Some lay the fault of the Disciples not understanding these things, upon the obscurity of our Saviours phrase, and his Parabolical expres<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sion of them: others in their ignorance of our Saviours Re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />surrection from the dead; others in their not understanding the circumstance of time; but certainly it is best imputed to the Disciples inability to conceive of these things, and the prejudices of their national error concerning the Temporal Kingdom of the <ns0:hi>Messias.</ns0:hi> Let it lye where it will, the weak<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ness of the Disciples may be reasonably conceived, not to be greater than is incident to the best of men; and if they were so dull of hearing and understanding, we may reasonably conceive, that we are not free from the like impotency and infirmity.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="19">19 Now Jesus knew that they were desirous to ask him <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">In the terms of this Verse there is nothing difficult, but in the matter of it there is much instructive: We learn from hence, That tho good men may as to some points be igno<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rant as to the mind and Will of God, yet they will be desi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rous of further instruction in it. To be willingly and con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tentedly ignorant, is not consistent with a root of saving grace. 2. Christ knows the desires of our hearts, before they are made known to him by the words of our lips; but yet it will not follow, that we may satisfie our selves with inward secret desires, without making them known by our lips; for God requireth the <ns0:hi>Calves</ns0:hi> of our lips, as well as the desires and groans of our inward man. 3.</ns0:note>, and said unto them, Do ye enquire a<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mong your selves of that I said, A little while and ye shall not see me: and again, A little while and ye shall see me <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">Christ is very ready to teach those whose hearts he seeth desirous to learn; therefore he saith, <ns0:hi>Do ye enquire amongst your selves? &c.</ns0:hi> Are you inquisitive? I am ready to teach, and to instruct you.</ns0:note>?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="20">20 Verily, verily I say unto you, that ye shall weep and lament, but the world shall rejoyce <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">Our Saviours reply is no litteral answer to their questi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />on, or exposition of the term which appeared so difficult to them to understand; but yet it is a substantial answer, by which he let them know, that he should be absent from them for some time, which time would be to them a time of mourning, and sadness, as he had before told them; that when the Bridegroom should be taken from them, then they should mourn; that time would be to the wicked part of the World, a time of mirth and jollity:</ns0:note>: and ye shall be sorrowful, but your sorrow shall be turned into joy <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">But their sorrow should be turned into joy when they shall see him again, both upon his Resurrection, and in the general Resurrection. The time of this life is the worldlings hour, and for the most part the <ns0:hi>power of darkness,</ns0:hi> to such as love and fear God; but as the worldlings joy shall at last be turned into sorrow; (they compass themselves about with sparks, but they shall at last lye down in sorrow) so the godly mans sorrow shall be turned into joy; Christ will say to the good servant, <ns0:hi>Enter thou into thy masters joy, Matth.</ns0:hi> 25.23.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>

                     <ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g>
                  </ns0:note> A woman, when she is in travel, hath for row, because her hour is come: but assoon as she is delivered of the child, she remembreth no more the anguish, for joy that a man is born into the world <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">Our Lord compareth the state of the Church in this life, and more especially in those first and most furious times, to the state of a woman that is big with child, and in her travel; when he saith, she hath sorrow, that is great pain, because God when he cursed the woman for her transgressi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />on, made this her porsion, <ns0:hi>Gen.</ns0:hi> 3.16. <ns0:hi>I will greatly multiply thy sorrow, and thy conception, in sorrow thou shalt bring forth children</ns0:hi>; and when her weeks are fulfilled, her hour is come to feel the effect of this curse, the fruit of the first womans transgression; but no sooner is she delivered of a child, but she forgetteth all her throws and pains, for joy of a child born into the World. Such (saith our Saviour to his Disciples) is your estate; you are as a <ns0:hi>woman in travail,</ns0:hi> so will all those that believe in me, be, to the end of the World.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="22">22 And ye now therefore have sorrow: but I will see you again <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">(The whole Church, <ns0:hi>Rev.</ns0:hi> 12.1, 2. is compared to a <ns0:hi>woman with child, crying, travailing in birth, and pained to be delivered</ns0:hi>); during this time of your <ns0:hi>travail,</ns0:hi> you must have sorrow. <ns0:hi>All those that will live godly in Christ Iesus, must suffer persecution. It is appointed for all men once to die.</ns0:hi> It is appointed for Gods people, (especially under some periods of time) to be <ns0:hi>dying daily, killed all the day long,</ns0:hi> as the Apostle expresseth the state of Christians in his time<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> 
                     <ns0:hi>Rom.</ns0:hi> 8 36. quoting <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 44.22. (which sheweth the state of the Church in the Old Testament to have been the same). But (saith our Saviour) it is but as the hour of the womans travail; it will be <ns0:hi>sharp,</ns0:hi> very sharp, but it shall be short:</ns0:note> 
                  <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 20.20.</ns0:note>, and your heart shall rejoyce, and your joy no man taketh from you <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">For <ns0:hi>I will see you again,</ns0:hi> and then your heart shall rejoyce; which cannot be understood of Christs seeing them again after his <ns0:hi>Resurrection</ns0:hi>; for before that time, we read of few or no sufferings of the Apostles or other Disciples. It must therefore be understood, either of the <ns0:hi>visitation of his Spi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rit,</ns0:hi> filling their hearts with joy and peace, or the <ns0:hi>visitati<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ons of his Providence</ns0:hi>; or rather of Christs coming to the last Judgment, when all that have believed in Christ, shall see him with joy unspeakable; and then <ns0:hi>all tears shall be wi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ped away from their eyes,</ns0:hi> and they shall enter into the joy of their Lord, and sigh and sorrow no more, nor shall it be in the power of all their enemies, to deprive them of their joy.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="23">23 And in that day ye shall ask me nothing <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">That the day here spoken of, is that before mentioned, <ns0:hi>ver.</ns0:hi> 22. when Christ promised to <ns0:hi>see them again,</ns0:hi> and that their hearts should re<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>oyce, is without question; but what that day is, (as we before shewed) is not so well agreed: Some understand it of the <ns0:hi>general Resurrection,</ns0:hi> when Christ shall come to judgment, when all askings for satisfaction as to any thing of which we doubt, shall cease; and this seemeth at first the plainest sense: you shall then be made perfect; as you shall want nothing, so you shall ask nothing. But because of the following words, which plainly refer to the time of this life: others distinguish concerning <ns0:hi>asking,</ns0:hi> and by asking here understand, <ns0:hi>asking by way of question,</ns0:hi> for further information, not by way of <ns0:hi>prayer</ns0:hi> for supply: and indeed the <ns0:hi>Greek</ns0:hi> word enforceth that sense; for it is not <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>, which signifieth to ask or beg, as in prayer<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> but <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>, which signifieth to ask for a resolution in case of doubting; now, tho it be true, that in the day of judgment when we shall see Christ as he is, and know God as we are known, we shall have no occasion to ask any questions; yet because the following words speak of an <ns0:hi>asking in Prayer,</ns0:hi> which is proper to this life; it should seem, that the day here mentioned, is <ns0:hi>some time before the last Iudgment</ns0:hi>: what that should be, is the question. It is certainly best un<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />derstood of the time after the effusion or <ns0:hi>pouring out of the Spirit</ns0:hi> in the days of <ns0:hi>Pentecost</ns0:hi>; of which time it was Pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />phesied by <ns0:hi>Ioel, Chap.</ns0:hi> 2.28. That God wou'd <ns0:hi>pour out his Spirit on all flesh: their sons and their daughters should pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />phesie, their young men should dream dreams, and their old men should see visions, Acts</ns0:hi> 2.17. and to which time <ns0:hi>Isaiah</ns0:hi> had a respect in his <ns0:hi>Prophecy, Chap.</ns0:hi> 11.9. that the <ns0:hi>Earth should be full of the knowledge of the Lord, as the waters co<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ver the Sea.</ns0:hi> So as these words, <ns0:hi>you shall ask me nothing in that day,</ns0:hi> signifie the great light that should upon the com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing down of the holy Spirit, shine in upon their Souls; so that they should no longer have any such doubts as they now had, and sound much the same thing that we have, 1 <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> 2.27. <ns0:hi>But the anointing,</ns0:hi> [by which is meant the holy Spirit] <ns0:hi>which ye have received of him, abideth in you: and you need not tha<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap> any man teach you: but as the same anointing teacheth you of all things.</ns0:hi> We must not too rigidly interpret our Saviou<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>s words here, as if they we<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>e a pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mise of such a state in this life, when either the present or succeeding Disciples of Christ should be so filled with know<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ledge, as they should have no further doubts, or need not to ask any thing of Christ, (that is, to be resolved in any thing). Our Saviour here speaketh onely <ns0:hi>comparatively,</ns0:hi> to signifie the great difference would be as to knowledge, betwixt them in their present state, and what should be after the pouring out of the holy Spirit; they should then fully un<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />derstand what Christ meant by his saying, <ns0:hi>A little while, and you shall not see me</ns0:hi>: and again, <ns0:hi>a little while, and you shall see me; because I go to the Father</ns0:hi>: and should not need ask him questions about that, or many other things which they were now at loss about as <ns0:hi>Ier.</ns0:hi> 31.34. where the Prophet saith, <ns0:hi>They shall teach no more every man his neighbour, and every man his brother, saying, Know the Lord: for they shall all know me, from the greatest to the least.</ns0:hi> It must not be interpreted (as some have done) to signifie a needlesness of Ministerial teaching; so neither must this text be interpreted, to signifie a needlesness of an inquiry of Christ for further satisfaction; but onely as sig<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nifying the vast difference in the degrees of knowledge, after the holy Spirit should be poured forth, from what was even in the best men, before that time.</ns0:note>: Verily, verily I say unto you, Whatsoever ye shall ask the Father in my Name, he will give <ns0:hi>it</ns0:hi> you <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">In the latter part of the text another word is used, it is not <ns0:gap reason="foreign">

                     </ns0:gap>. Our Saviour there plainly speaketh of their asking in Prayer; and their promise is, that to supply their defects of their knowledge, and the want of his personal instruction, they should obtain by Prayer from the Father, all that was ne<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cessary for their discharge of the Propheti<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">

                     </ns0:gap>al Office, <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 7.7. <ns0:hi>Chap.</ns0:hi> 15. <ns0:hi>ver.</ns0:hi> 7. <ns0:hi>Chap</ns0:hi> 16.24. See the notes on those Texts.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="24">24 Hitherto have ye asked nothing in my name <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">All the Prayers of believers under the Old Testa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ment were accepted upon the account of the Mediator, who was Typified by the Temple, and the Ark, where their solemn Worship was performed by Divine appointment. But the explicit naming of him, was not usual in their requests. Indeed the Prophet <ns0:hi>Daniel</ns0:hi> enforced his requests for the Lords sake<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> which may peculiarly respect the Me<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ias, the promised Mediator. Our Saviour in the form of Prayer dicta<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ted to his Disciples, gave no direction of addressing them<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />selves to God in his name. But now he was ready to ac<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />complish the Will of his Father, by offering himself as an expiatory Sacrifice for sin, and thereby reconciling God <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>o them; and the prevalency of his Intercession depending upon his Meritorious all-sufficient sufferings; he directs and incourages them to pray with an humble confidence in his name, for all the blessings they stand in need of. And 'tis matter of exceeding joy, that notwithstanding their unwor<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />thiness of the least favours, yet they are assured of obtain<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing their petitions offered up in his name: for the Father was so pleased with his voluntary obedience to the death of the Cross, that no blessing is so good or great, but he most willingly bestows for his sake to all humble suppli<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cants.</ns0:note>: ask, and ye shall receive <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 15.11.</ns0:note>; that your joy may be full <ns0:hi>t.</ns0:hi>
